passage:
At the Monday meeting in the small branch office above the fertiliser shop, Gautam Sir read out the collection figures and clapped for Mahesh. 'No excuses, no questions. That's how you get to district level.'
Jaya kept her eyes on her register. Two months ago she had asked, politely, whether the evening visits to borrowers' homes were becoming too harsh. The next week she was moved to the far villages with the worst roads and the smallest targets, and she stopped being invited to tea with the team.
Now Mahesh caught her eye and grinned. The team had covered for her when her mother was ill. She owed them.
Her father's pension didn't stretch far. This job did.
When Gautam Sir asked, 'Any concerns?', Jaya said nothing, and hated how easy it was.

qa.q: Where was Jaya moved after she asked her question?
qa.a: She was moved to the far villages with the worst roads and the smallest targets.

qa.q: Why does Jaya stay silent when Gautam Sir asks for concerns?
qa.a: She fears losing a job her family relies on and feels she owes the team, so loyalty and fear outweigh her unease, which she hates.

qa.q: What turning point is still available to Jaya at this stage?
qa.a: She could write down what she has seen and find one trusted colleague or an official channel to raise the harsh visits, so she is not carrying it alone.

qa.q: How might the borrowers be affected by a team where no one questions the visits?
qa.a: They may face growing pressure at home in the evenings with nobody inside the branch willing to speak up for fair treatment.

grounding: It shows a manager praising unquestioning results and sidelining a worker who raised a concern, so loyalty and job fear keep her silent.

passage:
In the site office in Johannesburg, the whiteboard had a new column: 'Delivered - no drama'. Omar, the project manager, added a gold star beside Zanele's name for finishing the third floor early.
'This is what I like,' he told the team. 'People who get it done and don't bring me problems.'
Nobody mentioned Thabo, who had asked last month why the concrete tests were being signed before the results came back. Thabo now did night inventory in the yard.
Zanele looked at her gold star and felt her stomach tighten. She had noticed the same thing as Thabo. She had said nothing.
Her younger brother's university fees were due in March. And the crew had been good to her, sharing lunch, covering her first mistakes.
She smiled for the photo Omar took of the board.

qa.q: What did Omar add beside Zanele's name?
qa.a: He added a gold star for finishing the third floor early.

qa.q: Why does Zanele's stomach tighten as she looks at her gold star?
qa.a: She knows she noticed the same problem as Thabo and stayed quiet, so the reward feels wrong even as fear and loyalty keep her silent.

qa.q: What turning point is open to Zanele at this stage?
qa.a: She could quietly talk to Thabo, note what she has seen, and look for a proper channel such as a safety officer to raise the concrete tests.

qa.q: What might Thabo be experiencing on night inventory?
qa.a: Thabo is likely feeling punished and isolated for asking an honest question while quieter colleagues are praised.

grounding: It shows a manager rewarding results without questions and sidelining the one who asked, while a young engineer stays silent out of fear and loyalty.
